headline: Sep 13 AM · The digest came back from the dead and had nothing to say. It fired on time at 15:00Z yesterday — the first AI-backed lane to speak since Sep 10 — and printed the same nine numbers for the fourth straight day: 0 new, 0 booked, 3 SLA-breached, 3 unbooked, 0% booking rate, median reply 135 min. So the blackout story narrows: the digest works, the FA-ADS watchdog is the lane still dark (56h), and the spend-sync alarm has now been silent 36 hours without ever once having said "success." Underneath the instrumentation, the fact that actually costs money is unchanged: Mary Grossman's callback window passed, and her miss is now confirmed by the scoreboard itself — 3 unbooked, 3 breached, 0 booked. Compliance 0/7 on day 17.
source: index.html · ORAYA DATA block v15.20 (2026-09-12) + live Gmail sweep Sep 12 14:12Z → Sep 13 01:05Z

spotlight.title: Mary Grossman — the miss is now on the scoreboard, not just missing from the inbox
spotlight.detail: Yesterday the absence of any call record was an inference from the mailbox. Today the system of record says it: the Sep 12 digest reads 3 with contact, 3 unbooked, 3 SLA breached, 0 booked. The first real $300-Plan lead (NV) asked for Fri 6:45 PM PT and nobody has written down what happened. She carries NO TCPA consent — hand-dial only, +1 805 302 2655. The board has now asked four mornings running for one sentence in a lane: called / referred / held.

spotlight.title: The blackout has a narrower shape than we thought — chase the watchdog, prove the sync
spotlight.detail: The Sep 12 digest firing at 15:00:06Z disproves "all AI lanes are dead." Two distinct faults remain. (1) The FA-ADS watchdog has not spoken since Sep 10 17:06Z — about 56 hours — so nobody is interpreting V2 spend. (2) The hourly Meta→CRM spend sync failed 14× on Sep 11 (00:32Z→13:32Z, 403 egress block) and has been silent ~36h since. It has never emitted a success notice in its life, so silence is not evidence of a fix. w30 is still the one-minute disproof: open the CRM and look for spend rows stamped after Sep 11 13:32Z.

spotlight.title: Day 17 of live consumer leads with a 0/7 compliance gate
spotlight.detail: Consumer lead flow went live Aug 27; seventeen days later not one of the seven blockers is closed. The two that actually gate the lead we already have are b3 (TX telephone-solicitor registration) and b7 (CA producer license #). Meanwhile the deciding metric — cost per booked call — has never once been measured, because the Meta→CRM feed has been broken since the day leads started arriving. Spending continues blind against ~$360 lifetime and zero confirmed bookings.
